## ai.proxy runtimes: how each harness consumes the resolved endpoint

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-25 — Claude's airlock route reads its
> service-delivered client token at launch, prepares current CA trust before one
> jail, pins Home Manager's config directory, and limits settings sources to its
> managed scope. CPA Claude uses `redact.assign` and the shared reader through
> `apiKeyHelper` for file, command and concat references, and clears inherited
> API keys, bearer tokens, custom headers and Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry switches in
> settings, and suppresses the inherited API-key descriptor before Claude
> starts. Codex uses command-backed provider auth. Resolved credentials supply
> owner-labelled Claude `/model` rows on both backends; airlock includes only
> the granted `api.anthropic.com` group. Codex discovers CPA models without
> per-credential profiles. Kimchi, Kiro and Copilot omit `proxy` support and
> warn.

### Claude (packages/claude-code/lib/proxy.nix)

An airlock instance keeps Claude's settings `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and
`apiKeyHelper` empty, and sets a visibly fake `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. The
generated launcher clears the early API-key descriptor. Before bwrap, its jail
permission reads only the selected client's token path from the rendered service
config, builds a percent-encoded `HTTPS_PROXY`, and combines current system
roots with the port-named `ca.pem` in a private per-launch bundle. It binds that
bundle read-only over the resolved system CA file with bwrap's `--ro-bind-data`
descriptor. A random private pathname is created and immediately unlinked; the
bundle is then populated through its open descriptor. Temporary traps remove the
pathname if creation or unlink is interrupted and preserve an existing jail
`add-cleanup` handler. The descriptor closes when bwrap exits. Missing service,
token, CA or roots fail the launch immediately. A selected Linux Claude requires
an enabled jail; config-only and non-Linux surfaces warn and deliver no airlock
launcher. Other runtimes reject airlock selections. A root airlock selection
therefore requires each enabled runtime inheriting it to support airlock.

The airlock launcher passes `--setting-sources user` on Home Manager and
`--setting-sources project` on devenv. Home Manager also pins
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to `$HOME/.claude`, where it delivers the user settings.
Both pass an explicit, non-secret `--settings` overlay with the static route
fields, including the fake OAuth token and empty base URL/helper. This keeps
unrelated settings in the managed scope while excluding other user, project and
local scopes for that invocation. It can exclude unrelated customizations from
those other scopes. Conflicting Nix-defined proxy environment keys and jail
environment overrides are rejected, including deferred jail permissions that set
or unset a proxy variable. A pinned Claude 2.1.310 offline probe observed the
competing CONNECT authority without the overlay and the restored
`api.anthropic.com:443` authority with the overlay for both user and project
settings. It also observed an empty helper suppress a lower-scope helper; it did
not inspect a real provider request or prove enterprise managed precedence.

A settings `env` beats the process env, so the endpoint travels through settings
files. `render` writes `env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (the origin; Claude appends
`/v1/messages`) and one strict `apiKeyHelper`. `lib/ai/proxy/key-helper.nix`,
shared with Codex, calls `redact.assign` with the selected file, command or
concat reference, then prints the resolved key with a constant `printf` format.
Its shell source carries only reference paths and concat's literal parts; the
secret stays in the shared reader's stdout and the helper's shell variable.
Resolution failures abort the helper before it returns a key.

Both `env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `env.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` are written blank.
Settings merge per key across scopes, so an inherited token or a lower-scope key
would otherwise accompany the helper's proxy key. An explicit
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` value also prompts interactive Claude, and declining sends
the claude.ai login instead (blank suppression probed on Claude Code 2.1.296).
`env.ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS` is blank for the same reason: Claude forwards
inherited custom headers, which can carry a credential.
`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` and
`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` are blank because an inherited switch sends model
traffic past the proxy; the live check measures both on the pinned CLI. Claude
Code 2.1.302 reads and caches `CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_FILE_DESCRIPTOR` before
applying settings env. A blank in settings cannot suppress it. A selected proxy
therefore installs a launcher through `lib.ai.mkLauncher` that unsets the
descriptor before exec; without a selection the package stays unchanged. An
explicit `ai.claude.package = null` keeps settings delivery and warns that the
caller must unset the descriptor when launching an unmanaged Claude.

Any selection also sets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` and
`DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` at `mkDefault`, and defaults
`settings.disableClaudeAiConnectors` to `true` to disable claude.ai connectors.

The endpoint lands in `native.settings`, so the settings.json the backend
already writes (user on Home Manager, project on devenv). The proxy leaves are
at ordinary priority, so a consumer's own value for one is a definition
conflict.

Each model of each resolved upstream credential (`normalized.proxy.credentials`)
becomes one `modelPicker.options` row,
`{model; description = "<credential> through <owner>";}`, where the owner is
CLIProxyAPI or airlock. Airlock supplies only the granted group intercepting
`api.anthropic.com`. `replaceBuiltInOptions` stays unset: Claude Code 2.1.306's
picker builder returns the built-in lineup plus each new row unless that flag is
`=== true`, and its schema says unset adds the rows after the built-ins. The
same schema says `modelPicker` is honored only from managed, `--settings`/SDK
and user settings, never a project checkout. So Home Manager writes the rows to
user settings, where a consumer's own rows concatenate, and devenv's launcher
adds `--settings <store file>` holding only `modelPicker`. Since the highest
scope that defines `modelPicker` wins outright, that devenv session shows the
credential rows instead of any user picker rows.

A row for a non-Anthropic id such as `glm-5.3` is listed and selectable in
2.1.306 (read from the bundle; the live TUI render was not observed). The row
schema has no model-name pattern, and the builder keeps a row unless its check
`H0o` fails, which is `One` (a retired Claude id) or `Xr` (the availability
allowlist) or `MF` (a first-party-only lookup that returns null off
`api.anthropic.com`); none rejects such an id. Gateway discovery keeps only ids
matching `/(claude|anthropic)/i`, which is why rows use `modelPicker` and not
discovery. Selecting a row passes validation before the server probe, so it
works while the proxy is down. A consumer `availableModels` that omits the id,
or a matching `deniedModels`, hides the row. Claude's handling of the unknown id
once selected (context window, effort defaults) is not covered; `behavesAs` is
the lever and the rows leave it unset.

### Codex (`packages/chatgpt-codex/lib/proxy.nix`)

One provider table per endpoint: `base_url` is the origin plus `/v1`, `name` is
the provider id (Codex refuses to load a provider without one),
`wire_api = "responses"` and `requires_openai_auth = false`. `true` would send a
ChatGPT login's token to the proxy. Every key becomes command-backed `auth`
through a strict helper that calls `redact.assign` and prints the resolved key
with a constant `printf` format. File, command and concat references share the
reader's failure checks; no resolved key is interpolated into shell or TOML.
Never `env_key`: tool subprocesses inherit it, and Home Manager's launcher
environment does not reach devenv's.

- **Home Manager** writes `model_provider = "ai-proxy"` and
  `[model_providers.ai-proxy]` into user config.toml. A devenv shell inherits
  the user file with no devenv configuration.
- **devenv** cannot use project config for providers: Codex strips
  `model_provider` and `model_providers` from project layers. Its launcher
  passes `-c model_providers.ai-proxy-devenv={…}` and
  `-c model_provider=ai-proxy-devenv`, the highest layer, baked in as
  `--add-flag`s. With `ai.codex.package = null` nothing carries them, so devenv
  warns.
- **Models.** Codex's `auth.command` provider fetches
  `<base_url>/models?client_version=`, which CPA answers in Codex's catalog
  shape (every registered model, unfiltered by client key), merged into the
  bundled list. Client routes still constrain requests. No per-credential
  profiles are written. `model_catalog_url` stays unset: it would replace the
  bundled list and empty the picker whenever CPA is down.
- **Availability tooltip.** Any proxy selection defaults
  `tui.model_availability_nux."gpt-6.1-sol" = 4` on both backends. Codex
  0.163.0's pinned source (`83086188`, `tui/src/app/startup_prompts.rs`)
  suppresses the startup availability tooltip once that model's shown count
  reaches four. Its bundled catalog announces only `gpt-6.1-sol`; the extracted
  catalog omits `availability_nux`, so this is a static default for that pin,
  not a claim about CPA's catalog. Consumers can override the count; other
  tooltips remain enabled.
- **A separate id on devenv is load-bearing.** Codex deep-merges layers per key,
  so session flags reusing `ai-proxy` could inherit incompatible user auth
  fields, such as `experimental_bearer_token`, beside the proxy's `auth`.

`chatgpt-codex-proxy` runs the pinned binary against loopback mock proxies in
the build sandbox. It covers all three reference forms on both backends, Home
Manager plus devenv precedence, and a legacy user bearer token beside a devenv
provider, with inherited `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CODEX_API_KEY` and `auth.json`
credentials that must appear in no request header. It also executes the helpers
directly with quotes, multiline values and shell metacharacters, and checks
failure output for leaks.

### Kimchi, Kiro, Copilot

Kimchi and Kiro omit `proxy` from `surfaceSupport`. They receive the standard
unsupported-surface warning, not a silent drop. Copilot is out of scope and
warns the same way. `ai-warnings-delivery` generates those cases from the
records on both backends.

### Checks

`packages/claude-code/checks/claude-proxy.nix` covers Claude on both backends:
key forms, precedence (quiet defaults yield, a consumer's proxy leaf conflicts,
nothing selected writes nothing, a selection does not warn), and the per-runtime
override. Its runtime check executes each generated helper with shell
metacharacters and multiline key contents, checks failure output for leaks, and
asserts inherited API-key and bearer variables are cleared. It also runs the
pinned CLI through both backends' installed launchers against a loopback capture
server with an inherited readable API-key descriptor, and checks that both
`x-api-key` and `Authorization` contain only the selected proxy key.
